event.title: Indian Police Detain Leaders of 'Cockroach' Movement Ahead of Protests
event.canonical_title: Indian Police Detain Leaders of 'Cockroach' Movement Ahead of Protests
event.summary: Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the 'Cockroach' youth movement, along with other leaders and hundreds of protesters at Delhi airport on October 10. This crackdown aimed to prevent mass protests against the country's election chief and a contentious voter list revision. Authorities imposed a strict lockdown in New Delhi, blocking thousands from attending the demonstration organized by the Cockroach Janata Party.

timeline.title: Protests in India Lead to Detentions Amid Calls for Election Chief's Resignation
timeline.summary: In Delhi, police detained hundreds of protesters for the second consecutive day as they demanded the resignation of India's election chief. The protests coincided with a court decision that resulted in the release of Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the 'cockroach' movement, along with two other senior leaders.
key_facts: Hundreds of protesters were detained in Delhi.
Protests were held for the resignation of India's election chief.
A court ordered the release of 'cockroach' movement leaders.

timeline.title: Indian Police Detain Cockroach Movement Founder Ahead of Planned Protest
timeline.summary: Indian police have detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, in preventive detention ahead of a planned protest in central Delhi. This action comes in response to his calls for a demonstration, which defies a court order banning such gatherings. The protest was organized following recent mass detentions and the jailing of two party leaders.
key_facts: Abhijeet Dipke is the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party.
Dipke was detained ahead of a protest in central Delhi.
The protest was called in defiance of a court order.

event_overview.title: About India Protests
event_overview.subject: India Protests
event_overview.summary: India’s 2026 “Cockroach” protests are a youth-led campaign associated with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which began online and later organized street demonstrations over education, employment and electoral issues. In its October phase, the movement and allied groups called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign over a large-scale revision of voter rolls; protesters allege improper exclusions, while the Election Commission has said roll revisions are intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: The CJP emerged as a satirical online youth movement in May 2026 and subsequently developed into an organizer of in-person protests.

facts.label: Protest agenda
facts.value: The movement first gained national attention through protests concerning alleged examination-paper leaks and youth employment; by late September and October 2026, its principal stated demand was the resignation of the chief election commissioner amid a dispute over voter-roll revisions.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The October campaign was organized across multiple Indian cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi, rather than being confined to one state or constituency.

facts.label: Election authority
facts.value: The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority that administers elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of president and vice president; Gyanesh Kumar became chief election commissioner on February 19, 2025.

facts.label: Legal framework for voter rolls
facts.value: Article 324 places preparation and control of electoral rolls under the Election Commission, while Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 permits the Commission to direct regular and special revisions of rolls; only eligible citizens whose names appear on a roll may vote.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the October 10-16, 2026 detentions and related demonstrations, not the movement’s full earlier education-focused campaign or every voter-roll dispute and protest nationwide.
